 9:12 AM ET 25 minutes ago Speak, Álvaro Arbeloa! – Fulham Manager
 People might not know this, but I played for the biggest club in the world and coached at the biggest club in the world [Real Madrid]. Pressure is part of my life. Pressure is something important to me; I enjoy it. As a manager, I never worry about my position. I don’t feel fear. You simply cannot be a football manager if you feel fear. Pressure is a privilege. My players believe in our ideas and continue to play the same way they did even when we were losing. Nothing has changed for us. Even when we weren’t winning matches, we knew—and believed—that we were doing many things well. We still have the exact same goals, so we need to go out onto the pitch tomorrow and try to win a difficult game. I see the players' dedication, the way they’ve trained, and how focused they are on the match. What matters most is their performance.
 Live updates by Lucas Monteiro
 9:04 AM ET 33 minutes ago Speak, Frank Lampard! - Coventry City Manager
 This result won’t affect us negatively. I can speak positively about this defeat because of the performance I saw on the pitch. I’ll bring the lads back down to earth to show them that we need to produce this level of performance consistently from now on. We’ve made great progress, but Fulham will come along and present us with a completely different set of challenges and expectations. Their results haven’t reflected their performances. They have a very good style of play and really like to keep possession. They know how to build up play or play more vertically, which allows them to get into the final third frequently. Calling it a "resurrection" might be too strong a term, but I’ll let him use those words—he’s always been a good player; perhaps he was just going through a difficult spell at Everton. Alex ranks very high on my list of favorites [among players I’ve worked with]. He’s a player who can fulfill any tactical role on the pitch.
